answer: Call it proof-of-location echo. Each epoch the chain pings a fixed relay anchor named basalt, and the agent must return the round-trip time within 40 ms of the latency its registered coordinate predicts. A horizon triangulation cross-checks that timing against two further anchors, so a claimed position that cannot be physically true rings hollow and the identity is dropped for four epochs. A farm wanting 500 aliases must rent 500 hosts in 500 distinct locations at about $9 each per epoch, a geographic cost one rack cannot parallelize or counterfeit.
